findings.text: UART_TI752_TCR denotes six for transmission control and UART_TI752_TLR denotes seven for trigger level, both as register offsets.

UART_TRG denotes zero where reads report fifo occupancy and writes set custom levels with feature control bit seven choosing receive or transmit, and UART_FCTR denotes one for the feature control function.

UART_TRG_1 denotes one and UART_TRG_4 denotes four and UART_TRG_8 denotes eight and UART_TRG_16 denotes sixteen and UART_TRG_32 denotes thirty two and UART_TRG_64 denotes sixty four and UART_TRG_96 denotes ninety six and UART_TRG_120 denotes one hundred twenty and UART_TRG_128 denotes one hundred twenty eight, forming rising custom trigger codes.

UART_FCTR_RTS_NODELAY denotes zero for no delay and UART_FCTR_RTS_4DELAY denotes one and UART_FCTR_RTS_6DELAY denotes two and UART_FCTR_RTS_8DELAY denotes three and UART_FCTR_IRDA denotes four for infrared select and UART_FCTR_TX_INT denotes eight for transmit interrupt type.

UART_FCTR_TRGA denotes zero and UART_FCTR_TRGB denotes sixteen and UART_FCTR_TRGC denotes thirty two and UART_FCTR_TRGD denotes forty eight for trigger table choice, plus UART_FCTR_SCR_SWAP denotes sixty four for scratch swap and UART_FCTR_RX denotes zero for receive versus UART_FCTR_TX denotes one hundred twenty eight for transmit direction.
UART_EMSR denotes seven for extended mode select, with UART_EMSR_FIFO_COUNT denoting bit zero for receive or transmit counting and UART_EMSR_ALT_COUNT denoting bit one for alternating count.

UART_IER_DMAE denotes bit seven for DMA requests and UART_IER_UUE denotes bit six for unit enable and UART_IER_NRZE denotes bit five for NRZ coding and UART_IER_RTOIE denotes bit four for receive timeout, while UART_IIR_TOD denotes bit three for timeout indication in the identity register.

UART_FCR_PXAR1 denotes zero for threshold one and UART_FCR_PXAR8 denotes sixty four for threshold eight and UART_FCR_PXAR16 denotes one hundred twenty eight for threshold sixteen and UART_FCR_PXAR32 denotes one hundred ninety two for threshold thirty two.
UART_ASR denotes one for additional status and UART_RFL denotes three for receiver level and UART_TFL denotes four for transmitter level and UART_ICR denotes five for index control.

UART_ACR denotes zero and UART_CPR denotes one and UART_TCR denotes two and UART_CKS denotes three and UART_TTL denotes four and UART_RTL denotes five and UART_FCL denotes six and UART_FCH denotes seven, covering control, prescalar, times clock, clock select, transmit trigger, receive trigger and two flow levels in order.

UART_ID1 denotes eight and UART_ID2 denotes nine and UART_ID3 denotes ten and UART_REV denotes eleven and UART_CSR denotes twelve and UART_NMR denotes thirteen and UART_CTR denotes two hundred fifty five as a guard, covering identifiers, revision, reset, nine bit mode and terminator.

UART_ACR_RXDIS denotes bit zero for receiver disable and UART_ACR_TXDIS denotes bit one for transmitter disable and UART_ACR_DSRFC denotes bit two for DSR flow and UART_ACR_TLENB denotes bit five for trigger levels enable and UART_ACR_ICRRD denotes bit six for index read and UART_ACR_ASREN denotes bit seven for additional status.

UART_RSA_BASE denotes negative eight as the anchor, UART_RSA_MSR denotes the anchor itself for mode select, with UART_RSA_MSR_SWAP denoting bit zero for low high swap and UART_RSA_MSR_FIFO denoting bit two for external fifo and UART_RSA_MSR_FLOW denoting bit three for auto flow and UART_RSA_MSR_ITYP denoting bit four for level versus edge choice.

UART_RSA_IER denotes one above the anchor for interrupt enable, with UART_RSA_IER_Rx_FIFO_H denoting bit zero and UART_RSA_IER_Tx_FIFO_H denoting bit one and UART_RSA_IER_Tx_FIFO_E denoting bit two and UART_RSA_IER_Rx_TOUT denoting bit three and UART_RSA_IER_TIMER denoting bit four, covering receive half, transmit half, transmit empty, receive timeout and timer respectively.

UART_RSA_SRR denotes two above the anchor for status read, with UART_RSA_SRR_Tx_FIFO_NEMP denoting bit zero and UART_RSA_SRR_Tx_FIFO_NHFL denoting bit one and UART_RSA_SRR_Tx_FIFO_NFUL denoting bit two and UART_RSA_SRR_Rx_FIFO_NEMP denoting bit three and UART_RSA_SRR_Rx_FIFO_NHFL denoting bit four and UART_RSA_SRR_Rx_FIFO_NFUL denoting bit five and UART_RSA_SRR_Rx_TOUT denoting bit six and UART_RSA_SRR_TIMER denoting bit seven, where set means not in the named fifo condition except timeout and timer which signal events.

UART_RSA_FRR denotes two above the anchor for fifo reset on output and UART_RSA_TIVSR denotes three above for timer period setting and UART_RSA_TCR denotes four above for timer control with UART_RSA_TCR_SWITCH denoting bit zero to switch the timer on.
SERIAL_RSA_BAUD_BASE denotes nine hundred twenty one thousand six hundred and SERIAL_RSA_BAUD_BASE_LO denotes that reference divided by eight.

virtio_balloon_config orders num_pages first for requested count and actual second for balloon count and a union third for command identifier and poison_val fourth, each as little endian thirty two bit words.

The third word is a union where free_page_hint_cmd_id and free_page_report_cmd_id name the same storage, the latter kept for legacy use, and poison_val carries the poisoning pattern only when page poisoning is negotiated.

VIRTIO_BLK_F_WCE denotes the same value as VIRTIO_BLK_F_FLUSH, namely nine, acting as an alias.
UART_RSA_BASE uses negative eight below the nominal base, so implementations must use signed arithmetic and must not let unsigned wraparound corrupt the small followers.
ASYNCB_BUGGY_UART requests skipping safety checks and is marked as risky, so it must only be set for known hardware and never speculatively.
The serial register header provides stable userspace offsets and bit codes for programming extended UART families including trigger, fifo, flow, mode and power functions.
The TTY headers provide stable userspace selectors for line disciplines and stable bit positions and masks for async port configuration.
The virtio headers provide stable guest host contracts for balloon and block features, configuration layouts and statistic tags.
